comment: Skills (stage 4F, ADR 0020, GDD 5.1): what people know, inside their stratum. A skill belongs to one stratum and is opened by one technology: the goods that technology adds to gathering come in only with its skilled people, and its recipes are worked only by them. People of a stratum without any of these skills are its plain members (gatherers among producers, warriors among warriors). jobsPercent: share of the stratum's people of a settlement the skill can use (full gathering of the technology's goods needs that many; apprentices are taken on up to it; a settlement whose recipe needs the skill can use all its artisans). trainingYears: years an apprentice learns. the jobs of one stratum's skills add up to at most 100%, so that every skill finds people (producers: farmers 50, hunters 20, fishers 15, herders 15; artisans: 75 in all, and a settlement's recipe can use all its artisans). rules: farmingSkill is the skill whose people farm a village's fields (GDD 4.4; the other producers gather); firstMasters appear when the civilization learns the technology, in its settlement with most people of the stratum; each master teaches up to apprenticesPerMaster; an apprentice works apprenticeWorkPercent of a skilled worker; skilled people move to a settlement of their own civilization within the trade link distance (data/trade.json linkCells) that needs them when their settlement has at least moveMinMasters and moveSpareAbove more than it can use, moveSharePercent of the spare at most, once per own step; while the civilization has settlements that need a skill and have no master of it, masters teach teachForOthersPercent more than their settlement can use, plus moveSpareAbove, so that skilled people can move; a civilization that lost a skill gets one master back per own step from a trade partner that has at least moveMinMasters. Elders (thinkers) and chiefs (leaders) come with their strata in PR 3.
